links.outcome: Agreement among medical experts rating summaries (reference standard variability)
links.effect: Average expert agreement was 19.2% among all experts and 54% among groups of 3 experts; GPT-4 agreed with at least 1 expert 83.06% of the time.
links.quote: The study found variability in expert consensus, with average agreement rates of 19.2% among all experts and 54% among groups of 3 experts.

unlisted_practices: LLM-as-judge automated evaluation of LLM-generated medical summaries against expert judgments
Prompt-enhanced guidance to improve LLM judge alignment with experts
Pairwise comparison to mitigate position bias in LLM judges

screen.reason: The study develops and tests an automated LLM-as-a-judge verification layer (using prompt engineering/prompt-enhanced guidance) to evaluate medical summarization outputs against human expert ground truth, directly testing an automated safeguard/verification practice.

primary.practice: LLM-as-a-judge auto-evaluation and prompt-enhanced guidance for verification
